proposalDescription: Configure background task worker (RQ/Celery/ProcessPoolExecutor) to recycle worker child processes after completing N heavy extraction jobs, immediately returning CPython/PyTorch heap allocations back to the OS.
pros: Zero code rewrite required for extraction engine or business logic
Releases 100% of retained PyTorch/CPython memory back to OS upon worker exit
Preserves high accuracy Docling table and OCR extraction capabilities
Can be controlled entirely via runtime environment configuration
cons: Slight process re-spawn latency (~150ms) on task N+1
decisionReason: Highly cost-effective non-rewrite solution that directly resolves the #1 memory retention bottleneck without risking OCR model regressions or incurring rewrite overhead.

candidateName: Rewrite Document Extraction Engine in Native Rust / C++
proposalDescription: Replace Python Docling/PyTorch document layout engine with a custom native Rust PDF parsing & layout analysis library.
pros: Instant startup time and minimal idle RSS (<50 MB)
cons: Extremely high engineering complexity and multi-month effort
High risk of severe quality degradation for complex PDF tables and multi-column document extraction
Violates modern workstream policy against speculative re-architecture
decisionReason: High risk and unnecessary; modular optional packaging and worker process recycling achieve all memory efficiency targets safely.

candidateName: Defer Heavy Module Imports (Lazy Dependency Loading)
proposalDescription: Defer importing PyTorch, Docling, and heavy ML packages until an extraction or embedding route is explicitly called, avoiding startup import cost during general API boot.
pros: Reduces Python backend startup time by ~350ms
Zero impact on non-extraction API routes or initial UI render
cons: First extraction request incurs initial module import latency
decisionReason: Simple Python architecture optimization that safely reduces API readiness time without full language or framework rewrites.

candidateName: Hold LLM Inference Layer & Rely on Native Host SSE Proxy
proposalDescription: Retain Python FastAPI streaming response handler for LLM RAG pipelines while using native Rust host reverse proxy for zero-copy SSE streaming.
pros: Native Tauri proxy delivers unbuffered SSE chunks with zero proxy delay (<1ms)
LLM inference performance is governed by underlying model provider / hardware acceleration
No changes required to existing Python RAG prompt pipeline contracts
cons: Cannot accelerate third-party or local LLM model inference rate through application code alone
decisionReason: RAG latency is bound by LLM model inference; proxy transport overhead is already fully optimized in the native Rust host.
